source.title: Non-uniqueness Phenomenon of Object Representation in Modeling IT Cortex by Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN)
source.authors: Qiulei Dong; Bo Liu; Zhan-Yi Hu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure values are available only graphically, not as readable numbers in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It tests representation similarity across independently initialized networks using explained variance, a different measure from the cited convergent-learning work.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports categorization accuracies, but those are not rows because they do not themselves measure representation similarity. It cites results from earlier convergent-learning studies; those cited results are not recorded as rows. The paper's theoretical propositions are discussed in authors_conclusion, not recorded as measured results.
record.test_reason: The study measures linear explained variance (EV) between penultimate-layer representations of same-architecture CIFAR networks trained from different seeds. It frames this as evidence and a theoretical argument for non-uniqueness, which bears on V3, V4, V6 and V7. This is T5 rather than T2 because the paper's purpose is to argue that equal performance does not imply equivalent representations.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right but should add the experimental findings. The authors show theoretically that equally performing DCNNs can have penultimate representations not related by a linear transform, so the goal-driven IT-modelling approach is inherently non-unique. Empirically, seed-trained pairs still show relatively large EV, which is larger for deeper nets. They urge care in choosing architectures when modelling cortex.
record.recipe_differences: Uses explained variance to assess representation linearity and tests CIFAR object-categorization networks; it is not a replication of the cited convergent-learning method.
record.method_sensitivity: EV varies with stimulus-set size before stabilizing around 3000 and is reported to vary with neuron-selection proportion, though the text is inconsistent about the direction. Added Gaussian noise up to σ = 0.1 changes EV little.

fits_no_version.finding: Scheme-2 constructs a second D1 network whose outputs are a nonlinear monotone transform of the first network's. It achieves similar accuracy with mean EV of 51.2%. Propositions 1–3 prove that such equally performing, non-linearly-related representations always exist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Equal task performance does not imply linearly equivalent representations; non-equivalent solutions exist by construction.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The supplied text does not give exact per-architecture EV values from the figures. The neuron-selectivity discussion gives conflicting descriptions of the direction of the EV trend. The study evaluates image categorization networks and does not test model scale, cross-modal alignment, alternative similarity metrics, or out-of-distribution data.
record.rows_left_out: Exact EV values for individual architectures and plotted conditions are not transcribed in the text and were not separately extracted from the figures; the text-reported aggregate ranges and qualitative figure results are recorded in r1, r2, and r4-r8.

untested.parts: No sweep over model scale or capability across different architectures, objectives or data. The depth trend (r8) concerns within-architecture seed pairs only.
Entire version; no vision–language or paired-modality data.
Only small CIFAR CNNs and only the penultimate layer. No feature-level or unit-level matching of its own; unit-level results are only cited from Li et al. and Wang et al.
Stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested. Cross-architecture mapping is argued theoretically only.
Entire version; no interpretable features or circuits are compared.
Only one similarity measure (EV) is used. No alternative metrics or neighbour settings, and no true out-of-distribution data beyond Gaussian noise.
No test of plateau, or of whether shared data or objectives explain the alignment.

record.verdict_notes: There is no real conflict in the neuron-selectivity text. EV rising with the included percentage implies smaller EV for the most-selective subsets. Exact per-architecture and per-noise-level EVs are figure-only and are declared in rows_left_out. The paper is primarily a neuroscience-modelling critique, with small CIFAR CNNs and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, nor comparison across differing architectures, objectives, data, or modalities as scale increases.
No paired image-caption representations or comparison of vision and language models.
Tests same-architecture networks with different random initializations on object categorization, not the range of architectures, tasks, or features in the version.
Tests linear representational similarity using explained variance; does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No interpretable features, neurons, or circuits are identified or compared.
Uses explained variance only; does not compare alternative similarity metrics or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Provides evidence about incomplete alignment, but does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives cause it.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs (D1, D2, D3, D5, D6)
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-10 object categorization; training scheme 1
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean explained variance between representations of networks with the same architecture and different random initializations.

conditions.value: Scheme-1; both networks trained with random initializations

rows.note: The paper reports this range across architectures, not separate text values for each architecture. It describes the EV as relatively large while stating that the representations cannot in theory be related by a linear transformation.
rows.check: Mean EV of 63.4–87.5% across D1/D2/D3/D5/D6 on CIFAR-10 reads differently per version. For V3 it is substantial shared linear structure, close to observed. For V4 it is partial, well short of a near-lossless linear map. For V7 it is observed, since alignment is incomplete.

source_check.correct: Mean EV is approximately 63.4–87.5%. States should distinguish versions: V3 observed substantial shared linear structure; V4 partial linear correspondence; V7 observed incomplete alignment, with causes untested.
source_check.problem: One partial state conflates shared structure, interchangeability, and observed incompleteness.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs (D3, D4, D6)
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-100 object categorization; training scheme 1
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean explained variance between representations of networks with the same architecture and different random initializations.

conditions.value: Scheme-1; both networks trained with random initializations

rows.note: The paper reports this range across architectures, not separate text values for each architecture. It describes the EV as relatively large, but the measured alignment is incomplete.
rows.check: Mean EV of 53.6–65.9% on CIFAR-100 is lower than on CIFAR-10. This is a weaker shared subspace and a clearly lossy linear map. It is observed incompleteness for V7.

source_check.correct: Mean EV is approximately 53.6–65.9%. V3 partial relative to CIFAR-10 and V4 partial are appropriate; V7 observed captures incomplete alignment, with causes untested.
source_check.problem: Partial fits V3 and V4 but does not describe the observed incompleteness relevant to V7.

rows.subject: D1 DCNN pair
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-10 object categorization; training scheme 2
rows.operation_detail: Trained the second network using a transformed penultimate-layer target and Euclidean loss, alongside the Softmax loss.
rows.note: This result comes from a deliberately constructed training procedure for the second network, rather than convergence arising from independent training alone.
rows.check: Scheme-2 deliberately trains the second network toward a nonlinear transform of the first network's outputs. The 51.2% EV is an engineered counterexample, not convergence arising from independent training. It should not be linked to V4.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs (architectures shown in Figure 2)
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 object categorization; training scheme 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared explained variance for all inputs with explained variance for only correctly categorized inputs.

conditions.value: only correctly categorized inputs versus all inputs

rows.value: The discrepancy is described as insignificant and negligible in most cases; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper attributes the small discrepancy, possibly, to the high categorization rate and the small fraction of incorrectly categorized inputs.
rows.check: This row is an input-subset comparison: correctly categorized inputs versus all inputs. The authors call the EV discrepancy insignificant and negligible in most cases, so it bears on V6's input dependence, not on V3 or V4.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs on CIFAR-10 (architectures shown in Figure 3)
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-10 object categorization; training scheme not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured explained variance on images with added Gaussian noise.
rows.baseline: EV without added noise; exact value not stated
rows.value: The paper says EV does not change much even at σ = 0.1; exact value is figure only.
rows.note: The paper reports that categorization accuracy decreases notably while EV changes little. This indicates representation alignment persists under the tested noise condition.
rows.check: Under Gaussian noise up to σ=0.1, EV 'does not change much' while accuracy drops notably. Measured alignment did not weaken under this input shift, so the state is absent for V6, not observed. V3 should be removed.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained for CIFAR-10 object categorization; training scheme not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured EV across resampled test subsets of increasing size.

conditions.value: whole test set, and separately correctly categorized images

rows.value: EV stabilizes when the stimulus set reaches around 3000; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The result indicates sensitivity to stimulus-set size before stabilization, with little change from further increases once the set is around 3000.
rows.check: EV stabilizes at around 3,000 stimuli. The text does not say in which direction EV moves below that size, so dependence appears only at small stimulus sets, consistent with estimation noise.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs (architectures shown in Figure 5)
rows.stage_stated: trained for object categorization; dataset and training scheme not stated for this analysis
rows.operation_detail: Measured EV between subsets of neurons selected by response-distribution kurtosis.
rows.value: The text says EV increases as the percentage of selective neurons increases; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The text also says EV between subsets of more selective neurons is smaller, which conflicts with its preceding description of the trend. The precise direction cannot be resolved from the supplied text.
rows.check: The text is not internally inconsistent. EV rises with the percentage of selective neurons included, so subsets restricted to the most selective neurons give smaller EV. Measured alignment therefore depends on which units are compared.

source_check.correct: The note should state that EV increases as more neurons are included; smaller subsets restricted to the most selective neurons have smaller EV. These descriptions are consistent.
source_check.problem: The row's note incorrectly alleges an internal contradiction; its verdict fix correctly resolves the wording.

rows.subject: similar-performing DCNN pairs (architectures compared in Figure 2)
rows.stage_stated: trained for object categorization; training scheme 1
rows.baseline: shallower architecture; exact value not stated
rows.value: The paper reports that deeper architectures generally have larger EV; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: This is a qualitative cross-architecture trend reported by the authors; it is not a model-size or capability scaling sweep.
rows.check: Deeper same-architecture pairs generally show larger EV. These are only qualitative figure values. This is not a scale sweep across architectures, so it does not bear on V1.
